correctness.rationale: The support face for a sign normal with k nonzero entries is a translated coordinate (k-1)-simplex times an orthogonal free (d-k)-cube; its edge Gram determinant is k, giving the intrinsic area and complete facet count. The area weights w(d,k)=C(d,k)*sqrt(k)/(k-1)! have exact consecutive ratio (d-k)/(k(k+1))*sqrt((k+1)/k). Expanding the log ratio on k=sqrt(d)+O(d^(1/4)), summing, and bounding tails by monotonic ratios gives the local Gaussian exp(-y^2)/sqrt(pi) and weak N(0,1/2) law; no finite experiment substitutes for this tail proof. The exact previously known volume V_d=2^d*sum_k C(d,k)/k! and the identity w(d,k)=k^(3/2) C(d,k)/k! give S/V ~ d^(3/4) by the same ratio concentration and uniform integrability. Independent finite weight ratio/count checks d=2..12 and scaled variances d=100,1000,10000 passed.

value.rationale: The natural canonical Euclidean sum has 3^d-1 facets but a surface-area typical rank of sqrt(d), unlike the count-typical 2d/3. Exact metric face-area spectrum, nontrivial local Gaussian profile, exponential count/area disparity and surface-volume power law are a motivated high-dimensional geometric phenomenon beyond merely re-listing facets.

final_claim: For Q_d=[-1,1]^d+B_1^d, all rank-k facets have area 2^(d-k)*sqrt(k)/(k-1)! and multiplicity 2^k*C(d,k); the surface-area-selected rank satisfies (K_d-sqrt(d))/d^(1/4) -> N(0,1/2), with local density exp(-y^2)/sqrt(pi), while count-typical ranks are of order d and S_d/V_d ~ d^(3/4).
limitations: Only canonical unit-scale Euclidean geometry, integer d>=2 and asymptotic d->infinity; not uniform in deformations.
